svg.text: Which terms matter, and which wash out

g.title: The paper ablates its own bound, term by term
g.desc: the paper ablates its bound term by term to see which contributions matter
g.text: Ablate the bound, term by term

g.title: Finite-rank error is an irreducible floor; residue terms shrink and vanish for large N
g.desc: the finite-rank error is an irreducible floor while residue terms shrink at a log-N-over-N rate and vanish for large samples
g.text: never vanishes, even with infinite data
Residue terms — shrink like log N / N

g.title: A ridge sweep shows the new bound improves toward the ridgeless limit while the prior worsens
g.desc: a ridge sweep shows the new bound improves toward the ridgeless limit while the prior bound worsens
g.text: isolating the ridge-dependence as the source of the gain

g.title: Dropping residues, the simplified bounds fail only in the small-sample regime, as predicted
g.desc: dropped the simplified bounds fail only in the small-sample regime as predicted and recover tightness as N grows
g.text: Simplified bounds stop bracketing only for small N —
exactly as predicted — and recover tightness as N grows.
